recent_posts.title: Making encrypted Java traffic observable with eBPF
recent_posts.summary: Coroot's open source node agent now supports decrypting and inspecting Java TLS traffic using eBPF. Java's TLS implementation (JSSE) runs inside the JVM with no exported native symbols, making it invisible to standard eBPF uprobes. The solution combines a lightweight Java agent (130KB) that hooks into JSSE's internal SSLSocketImpl classes with a stub native function that eBPF uprobes can attach to. Plaintext is copied to a native buffer before encryption, the stub is called, and eBPF captures the data along with the file descriptor via the subsequent syscall. Benchmarks show only a 15% CPU overhead compared to 38% for the OpenTelemetry Java agent, with no throughput degradation. Current limitations include SSLSocket-only support (no SSLEngine/Netty), HotSpot JVMs only, and a deprecation warning on Java 21+. The feature is disabled by default and must be explicitly enabled.

recent_posts.title: JDKProvider Gradle Plugin
recent_posts.summary: A new Gradle plugin called JDKProvider addresses compatibility issues with Windows ARM and JavaFX bundled JDKs. The plugin solves problems where Gradle toolchains don't recognize bundled JavaFX distributions and randomly select incompatible JDKs. It supports creating jpackaged applications, native applications, and multi-release JARs, with integration test samples available in the GitHub repository.

recent_posts.title: Java desktop app with Vue.js
recent_posts.summary: Learn how to build cross-platform desktop applications by combining a Vue.js frontend with a Java backend using JxBrowser's embedded Chromium engine. The approach enables modern web UI development while maintaining native filesystem access, offline capabilities, and seamless JavaScript-Java communication without requiring native toolkit rewrites.

recent_posts.title: FJDK - Flavours JDK | Manager
recent_posts.summary: FJDK is an open-source CLI tool written in Bash that manages multiple JDK installations without affecting the global system. It handles installation from Azul Zulu API or local files with SHA256 verification, allows switching between Java versions globally or per workspace, and provides isolated environments for different projects. Key features include workspace management with folder associations, automatic PATH configuration, fail-fast validation for missing JDKs, and an interactive fzf-based menu for navigation.

recent_posts.title: TDD as a Thinking Tool: My Opinion on the Practice
recent_posts.summary: A mid-level Java engineer reflects on the evolution of their relationship with Test-Driven Development, exploring the gap between TDD theory and practice in the software development community. The piece examines TDD as a thinking tool that fundamentally changes how developers approach software design, inspired by a provocative question about whether developers truly practice TDD and grounded in Kent Beck's foundational principles.

recent_posts.title: Agile Principles and Methodologies
recent_posts.summary: The author has completed the Agile Principles and Methodologies course from Codecademy, which has transformed their approach to frontend development projects. They learned about Agile mindset, Scrum roles and sprints, Kanban boards, and value-first delivery, enabling them to deliver software more effectively and efficiently across various projects.

recent_posts.title: Contacts Microservices Application with Asynchronous Communication with RabbitMQ
recent_posts.summary: The Contacts Application showcases a modern approach to building microservices with clear responsibilities and scalable architecture. It emphasizes asynchronous communication with RabbitMQ, clean architecture principles, and practical backend functionalities. The project uses HexaLayered Architecture, modern technologies like Java 17, Spring Boot 3.4.x, PostgreSQL, Liquibase, Docker, Mapstruct, Lombok, and TDD, and provides API interaction and documentation through Postman.

recent_posts.title: Downloading Gradle Artifacts using Git without an Artifact Repository
recent_posts.summary: A new Gradle Plugin named gitle allows users to clone and install artifacts directly from Git repositories. It builds the artifacts from source and publishes them to the local Maven repository, eliminating the need to publish artifacts to Maven Central.

recent_posts.title: Factory Design Pattern
recent_posts.summary: The Factory Design Pattern is a creational pattern that centralizes object creation logic, providing a way to instantiate objects without exposing the instantiation details to the client. This promotes loose coupling, easier maintenance, and extensibility. A real-world example in a healthcare ERP system demonstrates how different reports (e.g., Pharmacy, Billing, Inpatient) can be generated using this pattern. The pattern is beneficial for runtime object type determination, decoupling client code, and centralizing complex creation logic.

recent_posts.title: 1JPM - Maven/Gradle alternative in 1 Java File
recent_posts.summary: 1 Java Project Manager (1JPM) serves as an alternative to Maven/Gradle, offering a unique approach by utilizing a single Java file to manage build configurations. This system allows configuration using Java code instead of traditional XML or Groovy/DSL files. The developer seeks constructive feedback and engagement on the project.

top_posts.title: what is Spring Security for real 🤔
top_posts.summary: Spring Security is a powerful framework for securing Java applications, handling authentication and authorization. It protects against vulnerabilities like CSRF and XSS, offers customizable security policies, and integrates seamlessly with other Spring projects. Features include security context propagation, custom authentication providers, method-level security, and configuring security headers for enhanced protection. A real-world example shows how to secure a RESTful API with role-based access.

top_posts.title: Spring Security - Cross-Site Request Forgery 🔒
top_posts.summary: CSRF (Cross-Site Request Forgery) is an attack where a malicious actor tricks an authenticated user into performing unwanted actions on a web application. This happens as browsers automatically include user credentials with web requests. The post provides a detailed explanation using diagrams, explaining how such an attack works and emphasizing the importance of implementing defenses like anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite cookies to mitigate risks. It also mentions that Spring Security handles CSRF attack prevention by default.
